pictures.scene: Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a man in a black fur hat sits at his counting table weighing money, pinching one coin between finger and thumb over the little gold balance while the heap of coins and pearls lies in front of him on the green cloth, his wife beside him in a red gown and a white headdress turning the leaf of her painted prayer book but with her eyes gone sideways to the scales, the shelf behind them stacked with books and a flask and an apple, and a round convex mirror on the table catching a window and the street outside, then jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury, …
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Maes, Old Woman Praying — an old woman sits alone at the corner of her table in a dark room, seen in profile with her worn hands folded tight together and her eyes lifted, a white cap and a plain black jacket over a striped linen bodice, the red cloth pulled across the table in front of her with her open book on it, her spectacles laid down on the page, a pen, an inkpot and one small book beside it, and nothing else in the room but a vase of pinks on the ledge behind her, truly i tell you, he said, this poor widow has put in more than all the others, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on, …
pictures.name: pd_maes_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Liebermann, The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple — the boy stands barefoot in sandals in a plain pale robe in the middle of the temple floor with his hands held in front of him, talking, and the teachers crowd round him on every side, one old man in a white head-cloth and prayer shawl sitting and leaning down towards him, another bent right over with his hand up at his beard arguing back, more of them pressing in along the reading desk at the left with their books open, the dark carved stair and the lamps going up behind, as some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, jesus said, …
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a whole countryside has come out into the wood to hear one preacher, hundreds of heads packed in under the trees, hats and white head-cloths and hoods, the backs of the nearest listeners filling the bottom of the picture, boys climbed up into the branches to see over the crowd, and in the middle the man in a brown robe standing with both hands out and his mouth open, pointing away past them all towards somebody else, jesus answered, see to it that you are not deceived, for many will come in my name, claiming, i am he, and, the time is near, do not follow them, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Matejko, The Battle of Grunwald — a knight comes straight at us out of the press on a white horse, a huge white banner swelling and twisting over his head, his sword swung up in one steel gauntlet and a lance driven across his chest from the side, the black eagle shield at his shoulder, his mouth open and his eyes wide, and all round him the fight is jammed shut, horses' heads with rolling eyes and gold bridles shoving in from the right, a spear and a halberd crossing the top, two old men pushed in under the horse's neck at the left with their bare hands thrown up, when you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed, nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, …
pictures.name: pd_matejko_the_battle_of_grunwald

pictures.scene: Bocklin, The Plague — the plague comes down a narrow town street riding on the back of a great black winged beast, a green-faced figure in a black robe sitting astride it with a scythe held out in one hand, the long black wings stretched right across the picture and the beast's spined tail hanging down behind, the people running away up the lane under the houses and one already fallen, and at the bottom of the picture a woman in a scarlet dress lies dead face down across the paving stones beside another body wrapped in white, there will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven, …
pictures.name: pd_bocklin_pest

pictures.scene: Delaroche, Joan of Arc Questioned in Prison — the girl is sitting on the straw of a prison floor with a chain locked round her wrists and another running from the wall, in a plain white shift and a black jacket, her hands pressed together and her face lifted and steady, and the great man has had his chair carried in and set down beside her, an old cardinal in a scarlet gown and cap with a gold cross on his chest, leaning across at her with his mouth drawn down and one hand flung out, a clerk at his shoulder in the dark taking down every word she says, but before all this, they will seize you and persecute you, they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors, …
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — out of the dark of the garden the friend comes right up against Him and takes Him by the shoulder and kisses Him, their two heads together in the one light, Christ's eyes lowered and His hands locked in front of Him, the other man's face creased and straining up at Him, the armoured soldiers already closing in from the right in black steel with their red sleeves and their hands coming over, and behind them a great red cloak flung up over the whole scene while a disciple breaks away at the left with his mouth open and his arms thrown out, you will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death, …
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Gerome, The Christian Martyrs Last Prayer — a lion has come out alone onto the raked sand of the arena and stands still with his head up, the black mane heavy on his shoulders, looking across the empty floor towards the far side, and behind him the whole bowl of the amphitheatre is packed to the top with people, tier above tier of little faces under the colonnade, the shut green doors of the gate below them, pitch torches burning on their posts along the barrier and sending up black smoke, the storm cloud lying flat over the roofline and one gilded statue standing up against it, and you will be hated by everyone because of my name, …
pictures.name: pd_gerome_martyrs

pictures.scene: Roberts, The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem — the whole city is burning away below in the hollow of its hills, flame running along the inside of the ramparts and one great column of smoke going up and bending over the top of the sky, the towers and the colonnades still standing white in the glare on the far side, and along the rock shelf in front the army is drawn up in a long line of helmets and levelled spears and shields with the standards going up among them, an officer out ahead with his cloak flying, while under their feet the people taken out of the city are heaped on the bare stone, clinging together, an arm thrown up here and there, but when you see jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near, …
pictures.name: pd_roberts_siege_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Flight into Egypt — the family is already on the road out of the country, the mother riding sideways on the grey donkey with her child held up against her shoulder, one arm locked round him and his small hand up at her neck, both their faces set forward and both ringed with gold, her cloak falling over the donkey's back to its knees, the bare grey crag standing up behind them against the deep blue with two little trees on its ridge, and the rest of the party walking alongside, keeping up, then let those who are in judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city, …
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_flight_into_egypt

pictures.scene: Bendemann, Jews Mourning in Exile — an old man in a deep red robe and a yellow head-cloth sits on the ground under a vine with his harp laid over against his knee, one hand still resting on the strings but not playing, an iron ring round that wrist with the chain hanging from it, his face turned away and his white beard down on his chest, and the young woman beside him has dropped her head into his lap and hidden her face in her arms, her gold braided hair under his open hand, they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations, and jerusalem will be trodden down by the gentiles, until the times of the gentiles are fulfilled, …
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Aivazovsky, The Ninth Wave — the sun is coming up through the wrack after a night of storm and the whole sky is on fire with it, gold on one side and bruised violet on the other, the clouds still torn and streaming, and out of that light a green wall of water is rolling in with the spray smoking off its crest, and down in the trough a handful of men are still alive on the broken mast of their ship, roped on and clinging to it, one of them up on his knees holding a red rag over his head and another with his arm out, there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves, …
pictures.name: pd_aivazovsky_the_ninth_wave

pictures.scene: Taull, Christ in Majesty — painted across the half dome of a mountain church, the Lord sits inside a great oval of blue ringed with red and white bands, one hand lifted with two fingers out in blessing and the other holding an open book turned towards us that reads i am the light of the world, His robe blue-green and silver with red hems and His bare feet coming down over the edge of the ring onto the band below, the letters of the saints' names running round the outside, a painted cloud on either side of His shoulders, at that time they will see the son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory, …
pictures.name: pd_taull_pantocrator

lines.text: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.
Truly I tell you, He said, this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.
As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,
As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.
Teacher, they asked, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?
Jesus answered, See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, I am He, and, The time is near. Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.
Then He told them, Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.
This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.
So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.
For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.
Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.
But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.
For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.
Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
Then Jesus told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.
For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.
So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.
And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.
